item.title: OSCP Review + Tips :)
item.description:
Introduction

I passed the OSCP in under a month, barely touching the course material, but I didn’t come in cold. I’d already passed HackTheBox’s CWES and CPTS and had hands-on pentesting experience, which shaped how fast this went and how I approached it. This post covers what labs were actually worth my time, what the exam is really like, and the tips I wish I’d had going in.

item.title: CWES Review: How Pokemon Cards Helped Me Pass the CWES?
item.description:
Introduction

What is CWES

The Certified Web Exploitation Specialist (CWES) is a hands-on web penetration testing certification from HackTheBox. It consists of two parts:

  • The Course Content: Complete HTB’s “Web Penetration Tester” Job Role Path first (20 modules, 279 sections, 22 days).
  • The Exam: Then take a 7-day hands-on exam where you attack a simulated environment and submit a commercial-grade report.

Why I took it

Three reasons drove me:

  • Practical Skills Over Theory: I wanted a cert that tested real exploitation, not multiple-choice memorisation.
  • HTB Labs Prep: My goal was to learn how to tackle web footholds in the more advanced platform HTB Labs, and the CWES path seemed like good preparation.
  • 5-year goal?: I set a 5-year goal back in 2021 to focus on cybersecurity after finishing my computer science degree. The CWES was part of that vision.
